Roll — Privacy Policy

Last updated: 11 September 2026

Roll is a food and body-composition tracker. This policy explains exactly what it collects, why, where it goes, and how to get rid of it. It matches the machine-readable declarations in the app's privacy manifest.

Where this policy says Roll does something, it is describing what the code actually does, not an intention.

Who we are

Roll is operated by the app's developer, contactable at the support address on the App Store listing. That address is also the contact for any request in this policy.

What Roll collects

Account data. Your email address and, if you enter one, your name. This is your identity in the app — it is what lets your data follow you to a new phone.

What you log. Meals and their ingredients, portions, calories and macros; body weight; body measurements; water. This includes the words you actually typed or spoke. When you describe a meal, the description itself is saved alongside the result, so a log can be re-read and corrected later rather than being reduced to numbers you can no longer check.

Health information you enter yourself. If you fill them in: blood biomarkers, diagnosed conditions, food allergies, diet type, and supplements. This is health data in the legal sense, it is some of the most sensitive information the app holds, and every field is optional. Roll uses it to adjust your targets — the reason for each adjustment is shown on your plan — and for nothing else. Leaving these blank costs you accuracy and nothing else.

Apple Health. With your permission, Roll reads: steps, active energy, resting energy, exercise minutes, body mass, body fat percentage, body mass index, heart-rate variability, resting heart rate, sleep, and workouts. It writes back the meals you log, and your body weight only when Health has no other source for it.

Most of that never leaves your phone. Five of those readings are uploaded to your account so that trends survive a new device: active energy, resting energy, steps, exercise minutes and sleep duration. Body mass, body fat, body mass index, heart-rate variability, resting heart rate and your workout history are read on the device, used to calculate your targets there, and are not sent to us.

You can refuse or revoke Health access at any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Health. Roll keeps working without it, using estimates instead of measurements.

Photos you choose to analyse. A photo of a meal is sent for analysis and is not stored by us, before or after the analysis returns. Before it is sent it is resized and re-encoded on your phone, which removes the embedded camera data — including location — so that never leaves the device either. What the analysis provider does with the photo it receives is covered under "Where your data goes"; if you would rather no photo left your phone at all, meals entered by hand are never sent anywhere.

Voice descriptions. If you describe a meal out loud, the recording is transcribed on your device where your iPhone supports it. Where it does not, iOS sends the audio to Apple for transcription under Apple's own privacy policy. Roll receives only the resulting text and never stores the audio.

Barcodes you scan. The barcode number is sent to Open Food Facts, a public food database, to look up the product. Where your app version makes that request from the device, they also see its network address; newer versions ask through our server instead, and cache the answer so the same product is only ever looked up once for everybody. Either way they receive a barcode and nothing else — not your account, and nothing you have logged.

Products you teach Roll. If a barcode is not in any database and you enter the product yourself, the product name, brand and its nutrition per 100 g are shared with other Roll users so the next person to scan that jar does not have to type it in again. This happens automatically when you save the product. Your identity is never shared with it: other users see the product, never who entered it, and the app combines several people's entries rather than publishing any one person's. Nothing else you log is ever shared with another user, and you can ask us to remove a product you contributed.

Subscription status. Whether you have an active subscription, via RevenueCat and the App Store. Roll never sees your payment details — Apple handles the transaction and we only learn whether it succeeded.

Device verification. To stop automated abuse of the AI features, Roll asks Apple to confirm that requests come from a genuine copy of the app on a real device. We store a device key identifier and a counter. This says nothing about you, identifies no person, and is used for nothing but blocking fraud.

Diagnostic and usage events. Records of how the app behaves and how it is used: that a meal was logged and by which method, that an analysis succeeded or failed and how long it took, that a target was recalculated, which screens were opened, which buttons were pressed, how far a screen was scrolled, and errors. Screen and button records are kept for a small random sample of use — roughly three in a hundred — which is enough to see where a screen loses people and far less than recording everything.

Events from one run of the app share a session identifier so we can see what happened before a fault. That identifier is regenerated every launch and is never stored on your device — it links events to each other, not to you across time.

These never contain food names, photos, weights, macros or any free text you typed. Screen and button names are internal identifiers, not what you see on screen. Diagnostics exist to tell us the app works, and you can switch them off entirely in Profile → Settings → Diagnostics — off means nothing is recorded, not recorded and withheld.

What Roll does NOT do

  • No advertising, no ad networks, no tracking SDKs. Nothing you do in Roll is linked to data from other companies for advertising or measurement.
  • We never use Apple Health data for advertising or marketing. Apple's rules forbid it and so do we.
  • We do not sell your data. Not to anyone, for any purpose, ever.
  • We do not use your logged data to train AI models. We have no interest in it for that purpose and no arrangement with anyone to use it that way. What the meal-analysis provider may do with a request it receives is a separate matter, set out below — we would rather tell you plainly than imply a guarantee we are not in a position to give.
  • We never share your logged meals, weight or health information with other users. The one thing that can be shared is a product you explicitly choose to contribute, described above.

Where your data goes

Supabase hosts the database and authentication, in Amazon's Tokyo region (ap-northeast-1) in Japan. Your rows are protected by row-level security, meaning a signed-in user can read and write only their own data. Japan is covered by UK and EU adequacy decisions, so personal data may be transferred there without additional safeguards.

The meal-analysis provider is Moonshot AI, which operates the Kimi models and is based in China. When you log a meal by description, photo or voice, that description or photo is sent to Moonshot to estimate the ingredients and macros, along with your diet type and any allergies you have declared — those are sent so that an ambiguous description is read the right way round, for example reading an unqualified "milk" as the plant version for a vegan.

What we send is deliberately minimal. Your name, email, weight, body composition, biomarkers and conditions are never sent, and neither is any identifier that names you. Moonshot receives a meal and nothing that says whose meal it is.

What happens to it there is not ours to promise. Moonshot's published terms allow it to use content it receives to "provide, maintain, develop, support, and improve the Services", and they state that a customer wanting restrictions on the use of content for training or improving its models must negotiate a separate enterprise agreement. Roll does not hold one. Their terms state no retention period. We are telling you this in plain words because it is the one place your data goes that we do not control, and you are entitled to weigh it.

This is also an international transfer outside the UK and EEA. By using AI logging you are asking us to make it. You can avoid it completely: meals entered by hand, and barcodes, never reach any analysis provider, and the app works fully without it.

Apple receives voice audio for transcription where your device cannot do it locally, and handles Health data entirely on your device. Apple also operates the App Store purchase and the device verification described above.

Open Food Facts receives barcodes you scan, as described above.

RevenueCat and Apple handle subscriptions and receive only what is needed to validate a purchase.

Legal basis and your rights

Where the UK/EU GDPR applies, we process account and logged data to perform our contract with you (providing the app); health data — both what you type and what Apple Health provides — on the basis of your explicit consent, which you give by filling those fields in or granting the Health permission, and can withdraw at any time by clearing them or revoking the permission; and diagnostics on the basis of legitimate interest in a working product, which you can object to by turning diagnostics off.

You have the right to access, correct, export or delete your data, and to withdraw consent at any time.

Getting a copy of your data. Write to the support address and we will send you everything held against your account. We will not ask why.

Deleting your account deletes your data. Profile → Settings → Account & data → Delete account removes your account and the data associated with it, including everything above. This is irreversible, so ask for a copy first if you want one. Revoking Health permission stops further reads immediately; meals already written to Apple Health are yours and are removed through the Health app. A product you chose to contribute to the shared barcode database stays, because it no longer identifies you and other people now depend on it — tell us if you would rather it were removed.

Retention

Logged data is kept until you delete it or delete your account. Diagnostic events are deleted automatically 90 days after they are recorded.

Children

Roll is not directed at children under 13 (under 16 in some regions) and we do not knowingly collect their data. A calorie-tracking app is also not appropriate for them without medical supervision.

Not medical advice

Roll estimates energy and macronutrient needs from formulas and from your own logged data. It is a guide, not a clinical instrument, and it is not medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Talk to a qualified professional before making significant changes to your diet, especially if you are pregnant, have an eating disorder, diabetes, kidney or heart conditions, or are cutting weight for sport.

Changes

If this policy changes materially we will say so in the app before the change takes effect.

Roll — the same document the app bundles, so the two cannot drift apart.
